text: When checking in, travelers often say 'I have my luggage here' — remind them that 'luggage' is uncountable, so we say 'a piece of luggage' or 'bags,' not 'a luggage.'
A polite way to ask about seating is 'Could I get a window seat, please?' rather than 'Give me window seat.'
When ordering, natural phrasing is 'I'll have the...' or 'Could I get the...' rather than 'I want.'
Waitstaff often ask 'Are you ready to order?' — a natural learner reply is 'Yes, I'll have...' or 'Could we have a few more minutes?'
When checking in, a natural way to confirm a reservation is 'I have a reservation under the name...' rather than 'I book a room.'
To ask about a later check-out politely: 'Could I get a late check-out, if possible?' rather than 'I want late check-out.'
A natural way to state a destination is 'Could you take me to...?' or 'I'm heading to...' rather than 'I want go to...'
To ask about the fare naturally: 'About how much will it cost to get there?' rather than 'How much money?'
A natural way to ask for a recommendation is 'Could you recommend a good place for...?' rather than 'Tell me good place.'
When asking for directions, a natural phrase is 'Could you tell me how to get there?' or 'Is it within walking distance?' rather than 'Where is it, tell me way.'
Dropped-auxiliary-verb pattern: said 'I have book it yesterday' instead of 'I booked it yesterday' or 'I had booked it.'
Missing article: said 'is that correct way' instead of 'is that the correct way' or 'is that right?'
Hello, I want to check in for my flight. I have book it yesterday.
